## Summary

I implemented the disposable-domain email blocklist so that `POST /api/owners` rejects owners whose email domain is disposable, returning HTTP 400. This follows the existing `InvalidPostcodeException` → 400 pattern in the codebase.

**Changes:**

1. **`service/DisposableEmailDomainException.java`** (new) — a `RuntimeException` signaling invalid request input, mirroring the other 400-mapped exceptions.

2. **`service/ClinicServiceImpl.java`** — added a `DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS` set (`mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`) and an `assertEmailDomainAllowed(Owner)` check that extracts the domain after the last `@` (case-insensitive) and throws when blocklisted. It's called in `saveOwner` right after email normalization, so both the normalized value and the comparison are lower-cased. A null email or one without `@` is left untouched (the `@Email` bean-validation constraint on the field handles malformed input).

3. **`rest/advice/ExceptionControllerAdvice.java`** — added an `@ExceptionHandler` mapping `DisposableEmailDomainException` to `400 Bad Request`, consistent with the existing `InvalidPostcodeException`/`FutureRegistrationDateException` handlers.

The acceptance test `errorRejectsDisposableDomain` (which posts `x@mailinator.com` and expects 400) passes, and valid emails on other domains continue through unaffected.
